scope_notes: Postgres-native durable execution engine (SQL schema + TS/Python/Go SDKs + absurdctl CLI + habitat web UI): workflow-engine. uses_llm=true because absurdctl ships and installs an agent skill (skills/absurd/SKILL.md, CHANGELOG.md:35) and is meant to be driven by agents; has_ui and network_service from habitat (HTTP on :7890); executes_code because workers run registered task handlers for tasks any caller (including agents via spawn-task) enqueues; distributed via npm, PyPI and GitHub release binaries. No crypto, no third-party content parsing, no heavy compute. Second-reviewer subset: 16 criteria only.

PUR-1.note: README states the problem (durable execution on Postgres only), how to start, the agent workflow, and a non-goal (no push model); docs/comparison.md lists what Absurd deliberately does not own; claim-expiry overlap is documented. No machine-readable capability statement (SKILL.md is prose).

PUR-2.note: No numeric headline claims, but the value framing ('simplest durable execution workflow system', exactly-once promise) and the opinionated comparison are unmeasured; no benchmark harness, results, baseline or overhead numbers exist in the repo.

COR-1.note: SQL-level integration tests against real Postgres plus TS, Python and Go SDK suites run on every push and PR via make check/test. Gaps: habitat Go tests are not run in CI (build.yml only builds), single OS (ubuntu-latest), no coverage measurement, ratio not reported by the project.

evidence: rg 'hypothesis|fast-check|quickcheck|gopter|mutmut|stryker|func Fuzz|fuzz' -> no test-strength tooling (only Math.random in examples)
COR-3.note: No mutation, property-based or fuzz testing anywhere; only hand-picked parametrized edge cases.

REL-1.note: Core purpose: step checkpoints in Postgres, claim leases with expiry and extension, spawn idempotency keys, bounded retries with capped backoff and max_attempts; CI tests simulate worker loss via fake-time lease expiry and verify checkpoints survive retries. Not 5: no process-kill fault injection, and overlapping execution after claim expiry is documented rather than prevented.

SEC-1.note: No SECURITY.md, no reporting contact, no threat model or trust-boundary statement (habitat listens on all interfaces by default with no stated exposure assumptions). Only a changelog line records a past security fix.

SEC-2.note: Lockfiles are committed and the SDK CI uses npm ci, but the release habitat UI build uses npm install (lockfile not enforced), there is no Dependabot/Renovate and no known-vulnerability scan in CI.

SEC-5.note: All 37 action references are tag or branch refs, including a branch-pinned publish action in jobs holding id-token: write. test.yml and most build.yml jobs set no permissions (repo default token). Mitigations: docs.yml top-level read, environment-gated OIDC publishing, no pull_request_target.

AGT-2.note: drop-queue asks for confirmation, cleanup and migrate offer --dry-run, and the skill tells agents which commands change state. Gaps: detach-candidate --drop drops a partition with no confirmation or dry-run, and the skill's state-changing list omits detach-candidate, cron and queue-policy; no read-only mode or scoped credential guidance; no machine-readable effect hints.

INT-1.note: Documented SDK APIs (TS/Python/Go), a partially documented SQL function interface and a documented CLI with a queryable schema version. The CLI has no JSON output, there is no MCP/OpenAPI surface, SDKs do not check the installed schema version, and no SDK/schema compatibility policy is stated.

evidence: grep -c 'raise exception sqlstate' sql/absurd.sql -> 15 of 80 raise sites
INT-4.note: Three custom SQLSTATEs (AB001 cancelled, AB002 run already failed, AB003 invalid retry strategy) map to typed SDK errors and are asserted in tests; the remaining raise sites are free-text messages with the generic code. No remediation or retryable fields; CLI exits 1 for every error; CONTRIBUTING's 'Error Payloads' section contains unrelated text.

EPI-1.note: Task and run records keep task params, headers, retry settings, attempt, claiming worker, timestamps, result and structured failure reasons; checkpoints keep owner run and time. No schema/SDK/task-code version or input digest is recorded with results.

EPI-3.note: dump-task states its search scope ('not found in any queue') and workers defer unknown task names instead of failing them. list-tasks prints 'No tasks found' without restating filters or limit, and fetchTaskResult documents null as 'task does not exist' for a single-queue lookup that retention cleanup can also empty.

MNT-3.note: Type checking runs in CI (tsc for the TS SDK and habitat UI, ty for the Python SDK; Go compiles), TS configs are strict. No linter is configured, and formatters (prettier, ruff format, gofmt) exist only as a local make target, not checked in CI.

EVO-1.note: Per-release changelog, a migration script for every schema version, documented upgrade path with --dry-run and --dump-sql, and CI checks SDK versions against the tag. Pre-1.0 versions with no stated versioning policy; behaviour changes are listed as 'Changed' without breaking labels.

PRV-3.note: Unmodified Apache-2.0 LICENSE with SPDX ids in manifests, a copy in the Go module and the OFL font licence kept with the font. No third-party notice file for the UI dependencies embedded in released habitat binaries (completeness of retained notices in the bundle not verifiable statically); no REUSE headers.
